input.question: Why is it such a "Taboo" to talk about how much you get paid at your job with co-workers?
input.ground_truth: Companies don't want you to know what everyone else makes. It's harder to value your own worth when you only know what you make. When people know what others make, they might be more likely to demand more. So, by making sure only you know how much you make (whether through contract language or through it being "frowned upon"), the company tends to get to pay people less

Okay! Imagine you and your friends are playing a game together. Some of your friends have more toys than others. If you all talk about how many toys everyone has, some people might feel sad or jealous because they have fewer toys.

Talking about how much money people get at their jobs is kind of like that. Some people might get more money, and some might get less. If everyone talks about it, some people might feel bad or worry that others will think less of them. That’s why it’s called a “taboo”—it’s something people usually don’t talk about at work, so everyone can feel comfortable and not compare or worry about each other.
